problems.description: The commit deletes the existing seed (index.ts Express Todo API, described as the baseline with 'good seams' for multi-session TypeScript stories) wholesale rather than building on or porting it, discarding the baseline structure the story was meant to evolve.
Jest + ts-jest are configured (jest.config.js, test script) but the commit ships zero test files, leaving the new generator and CLI uncovered at session 1.

FLAGGED DISCREPANCY: the 31 violations and 0.47 convention score cite rules like 'Functions should not use snake_case' and 'Classes should use PascalCase' against code that already uses camelCase/PascalCase — this reads like a Python-tuned linter misapplied to TypeScript, so the measured score likely understates real convention adherence.
The project is renamed to 'ssg' with new deps (marked, gray-matter) and no lockfile is committed, so dependency resolution is non-reproducible.

strengths: Clean modular layering: cli.ts handles arg parsing/entry, generator.ts holds the build core, plus a separate dev-server plugin — clear separation of concerns for an SSG.
Defensive data handling: frontmatter values are normalized (tags split/coerced, dates normalized) and all user content is HTML-escaped before output.
Zero SonarQube bugs, smells, or duplication, with only a modest +9 cognitive complexity delta — the new code is small and readable.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, well-layered greenfield static-site generator, but it discards the seeded Express baseline entirely and ships test infrastructure with zero tests; the 0.47 convention score appears to come from a language-mismatched checker, not the actual TypeScript.

problems.description: Hand-rolled regex-based template engine in renderTemplate (generator.ts) cannot correctly parse nested blocks of the same type (e.g. {{#if a}}{{#if b}}{{/if}}{{/if}}) because non-greedy regex stops at the first closing tag, leaving orphaned tags; the project already depends on `marked`, so a real template library (e.g. handlebars) would be more robust than a regex parser.

renderTemplate implements two template dialects (Handlebars {{#each}}/{{#if}}/{{>partial}} and EJS <% include() %>/<%= %>) in one engine, doubling the syntax surface and partial-resolution paths; should standardize on one dialect.

The diff adds +150 lines including a new template/partial/layout renderer with no visible tests; the +3 functions (valueAt, renderTemplate, loadPartials, renderPage — 4 by my count) are untested given AST measurements show no test file additions.

Cognitive complexity +4 from the nested regex-replacement pipeline in renderTemplate; the sequential string-replace approach makes control flow and ordering (each before if before partials before interpolation) hard to reason about and extend.

Convention score 0.47 appears to be repo-wide, not commit-introduced: listed violations include dev-server-plugin.ts, which is not in this diff, and cli.ts snake_case/PascalCase items that the added camelCase code does not match; flagging discrepancy between measurement scope and commit scope.

strengths: Feature slots cleanly into existing architecture: CLI flag → BuildOptions → generator, mirroring the established --content/--output option-handling pattern exactly.
New code follows repo conventions: camelCase functions, PascalCase interfaces (BuildOptions, TemplateContext), optional fields, and reuses the existing escapeHtml helper.
Defensive, fail-fast behavior: throws on missing template/layout files and falls back to pageDocument()/default template instead of silently producing empty output.
Supports subdirectory layouts (templates/layouts) and extension inference (.hbs/.ejs) with graceful fallback, showing reasonable forward compatibility.
Security-conscious default: interpolations are HTML-escaped by default with explicit triple-mustache for raw output.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, convention-respecting feature addition that fits the existing CLI→generator pipeline, but the hand-rolled regex template engine (+4 cognitive complexity, untested) introduces maintainability debt that a library like handlebars would avoid.

problems.description: DISCREPANCY: measured convention score is 0.47 with 31 violations, but the cited violations do not match the diff. cli.ts and dev-server-plugin.ts contain no classes, interfaces, or constants that could violate PascalCase/UPPER_CASE, and all functions are already camelCase. The analyzer appears to be flagging false positives (likely misconfigured for TypeScript). Qualitative review finds the code actually adheres to the conventions.

Live reload is injected at build time by rewriting generated HTML files in DevServerPlugin.afterBuild rather than being served by the dev server; this couples build output to serve behavior and re-writes files on every build even when serving is not in use.

SonarQube reports +4 smells and cognitive complexity +3, consistent with the nested template-string interpolation in injectLiveReload and the inlined liveReloadScript HTML; extracting the script into a constant would reduce it.

The new --config option is threaded through parseArgs into BuildOptions, but the truncated diff shows no consumer of the config value in the build pipeline, suggesting it may be a vestigial/unwired option.

strengths: Refactor cleanly extracts rendering concerns into MarkdownPlugin/TemplatePlugin, shrinking generator.ts by ~196 lines while keeping the public Plugin seam intact
DevServerPlugin is self-contained with a narrow DevServerPluginOptions type and composes cleanly via the existing afterBuild hook
New public API (Plugin, PluginModule, PluginContext, all plugins) is properly re-exported through generator.ts
TypeScript typing is consistent throughout — type-only imports, explicit return types, and no new dependencies
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally sound plugin extraction that respects the existing Plugin seam and improves modularity (net -196 lines), but the measured convention score of 0.47 is a false positive — the reported violations contradict the actual diff, which follows camelCase/PascalCase conventions correctly.

problems.description: BuildPages = Page[] & { stats } mutates a plain array to carry metadata; cli.ts reads pages.stats at runtime, which is undefined if the array isn't Object.assign'ed with stats, and the return type change breaks the prior buildSite contract (callers expecting Page[] get a subtype with undocumented extra props). Return { pages, stats } instead.

Cognitive complexity +29 (per SonarQube) concentrated in buildSite and the nested templateHash recursion; incremental invalidation logic is inlined into the core build loop rather than isolated behind a cache module.

setParsedPageData is exported from markdown-plugin and invoked by generator.ts for every page, coupling the generator to plugin internals and duplicating the plugin hook's responsibility; frontmatter/content handling should stay inside the MarkdownPlugin.

.ssg-cache.json is written to path.dirname(outputDir) (the parent of the output dir) rather than the output dir or a conventional cache location, which can fail on non-writable parents and is surprising to discover.
templateHash walks and hashes every template file on every build even when the previous cache is already valid and matches.

Convention score 0.47 with 31 violations; most listed violations (PascalCase/UPPER_CASE in cli.ts, dev-server-plugin.ts) appear pre-existing or unrelated to this diff — new symbols (BuildStats, CachePage, BuildCache, templateHash) follow camelCase/PascalCase, so the low score likely reflects baseline state rather than this commit.

strengths: Cache invalidation is soundly keyed on source hash + template hash with a versioned cache schema
Feature reuses the existing plugin context (build.changedOutputs, stats) rather than introducing a parallel subsystem
Stats surfaced to the CLI output give users visibility into skipped builds and time saved
commit_reviews.summary: A functional incremental-build feature that reuses the plugin context well but introduces a fragile array-with-metadata return type, +29 cognitive complexity, and generator-to-plugin coupling, landing slightly below the codebase's conventions (0.47).

compounding_issues: Hand-rolled regex template engine supporting both Handlebars and EJS dialects (created in Session 2) persisted through Session 5 instead of adopting handlebars/ejs; increasingly ad-hoc and fragile in template-plugin.ts

Session 4's plugin lifecycle interface lacked a caching hook, so Session 5 had to bolt on setParsedPageData() + module-level WeakMap state (pageMetadata/parsedPages) to thread incremental-cache data through the plugin seam — a hidden cross-module coupling
The 93-line seed index.ts prototype was discarded entirely in Session 1 rather than evolved, wasting the seed as a throwaway
key_decisions: Session 1: discard the seed and rebuild as a typed TypeScript project (package.json, tsconfig, jest, src/cli.ts, src/generator.ts, tests)
Session 2: build a custom dependency-free template engine with templatesDir, template/layout frontmatter, partials, and escaped/unescaped output
Session 3: integrate a WebSocket live-reload dev server (src/server.ts) using ws + chokidar with a serve CLI command

Session 4: extract a plugin architecture (Plugin lifecycle hooks onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd, markdown/template/dev-server plugins, ssg.config.ts plugin loading) — the most consequential choice, cutting generator.ts by ~224 lines

Session 5: content-hash incremental build cache (.ssg-cache.json manifest, per-page sha256 source + template-hash invalidation, BuildStats pagesBuilt/pagesSkipped/timeSaved, --incremental/--clean flags)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily and coherently across all five sessions. Each session added a well-tested, vertically integrated layer — foundation in Session 1, templating in Session 2, dev server in Session 3, plugin architecture in Session 4, and incremental caching in Session 5 — with the test suite growing in lockstep (43 to 200+ lines covering templates, escaping, incremental rebuilds, and clean builds). Session 4 was a genuine structural improvement (net -263 lines, cleaner separation of concerns) rather than churn, and Session 5 built naturally on that plugin seam, delivering a content-hashed incremental cache as a capstone. The only flat spot is the inherited hand-rolled template engine and the WeakMap/setParsedPageData backdoor introduced to make caching work through the plugin interface.
story_review.summary: A near-textbook coherent progression from a throwaway prototype to a plugin-based static site generator with live-reload dev server and incremental builds, marred only by a persistent custom template engine and a plugin-interface seam that Session 5 had to work around.
